CURRENT BUSINESS QUESTION
Assess the US pilot of Harbor Relay (launch 21 Oct 2026), which sends an account activity report to the customer, retained 30 days and openable only by the customer, for privacy/data-access and related considerations — including whether support staff may open reports.
Edit question
Earlier questions
USEFUL CURRENT ANSWERBased on an earlier question or source

Source: Saved matter answer

Current answer

The saved fact stands as reported: Sam Patel reports that support can open a report only for a customer support ticket, and every access is logged. It remains active and reported (verification status: reported) — not independently verified. It answers the open supporting question Q-support-access: support can open reports, but only under a defined condition (a customer support ticket) and with logging.

What changed
The access question is now effectively answered. The earlier open question — "Can support staff open reports, and under what conditions?" — is resolved by this reported fact: yes, but only for a customer support ticket, with every access logged.
A material conflict now exists between the supplied specification and the reported business reply. The supplied spec (harbor-spec-v1.txt) states "Support staff cannot open report content." Sam Patel's report says support can open reports (for tickets, logged). These directly contradict each other as reported. This is the key new point — it's no longer just a tension with the "only the customer can open" phrasing; the spec affirmatively states support cannot open report content at all.
The two open working assumptions remain open but are now sharper: the spec's access statement needs reconciling with the reported conditional support access, and the privacy/data-access implications of that support access (even logged and ticket-gated) still need assessment.
What has not changed
No legal decision recorded; no draft created. The matter remains in intake/orientation.
The fact's status stays active and reported — it is not upgraded to verified.
The spec document, facts, and decisions are unchanged.
Note on the conflict

Because the supplied spec ("Support staff cannot open report content") and Sam Patel's report (support can open for tickets, logged) conflict as reported, the next useful step is to confirm which reflects the intended access model — or to treat the spec as needing an update to describe the conditional support access. I have not changed the spec, facts, or decisions. Would you like me to prepare wording to reconcile the spec's access statement, or to confirm the access model with the product owner?

Here is my reassessment of the reported fact change. No documents, facts, or decisions have been changed.

What changed

The fact record for Sam Patel's report was consolidated. The earlier fact the internal record ("Sam Patel reports that support can open a report only for a customer support ticket and every access is logged") is now superseded by the internal record, which carries the same substance plus an explicit qualification: it "remains reported, not independently verified; the supplied version 2 is consistent with the report."

What changed in the reasoning and why
The substance of the reported fact is unchanged. The core claim — support can open a report only for a customer support ticket, and every access is logged — is identical between the superseded and current fact. No new behavioral fact was added.
What is new is the explicit linkage to spec v2. The current fact now states that the supplied version 2 is consistent with Sam Patel's report. This is the material reasoning change: v2's access model (customers and support staff; support requires a ticket and is logged) matches the reported ticket-only, logged support access. That consistency strengthens the plausibility of the report as reflecting the intended model.
The verification status is deliberately unchanged. The fact is still reported, not independently verified. The consistency with v2 does not upgrade it to verified — it means the current supplied specification says the same thing Sam Patel reported. This is the correct treatment: spec text is supplied material, not independent verification.
Why the conclusion stays the same
The support-access question is effectively answered at the reported/spec level. Both the reported fact and v2 now point to the same model: ticket-only, logged support access. The earlier conflict — where v1 said "support staff cannot open report content" while Sam Patel reported support can open reports — is resolved by v2, which aligns with the report.
The open items remain open. The 180-day retention rationale, whether the ticket-gating/logging is implemented as described, and whether v2 is final are all still unverified. The reported-not-verified qualification is preserved, so no conclusion is upgraded.
Historical scenarios (comparison only)
The earlier v1-based scenario treated support access as unconfirmed and the "only the customer can open" statement as a promise needing reconciliation. That framing is now superseded by v2, which specifies support access and drops the customer-only language. This is a comparison, not a current fact.
The v2-based scenario (the current supplied record) treats ticket-only, logged support access as the operative model, consistent with Sam Patel's report. This is where the reasoning now sits.
Bottom line

The fact's substance is unchanged; what changed is the explicit note that v2 is consistent with the report, which resolves the earlier v1-vs-report conflict at the supplied-spec level. The conclusion stays the same: support access is reported as ticket-only and logged, consistent with v2, but remains not independently verified, and the retention rationale and implementation details remain open. No documents, facts, or decisions were changed.

Here's my initial advice on the Harbor Relay US pilot.

Initial advice — Harbor Relay account activity report

What you've told me: A US pilot of Harbor Relay launches 21 October 2026. The product sends an account activity report to the customer, retained 30 days, and the supplied spec says only the customer can open it. Business hasn't confirmed whether support staff can open reports. Working assessment (preliminary, no authority retrieved): The report almost certainly contains customer transaction/account data, so the two design choices you've flagged — 30-day retention and customer-only access — are privacy and data-access controls, not just product features. The material question is whether the "only the customer can open" statement is an accurate description of the product's actual access model.

If support staff can open reports, then the spec's "only the customer can open them" is inaccurate as written, and you'd want to reconcile it before the pilot. That's not necessarily a blocker — support access under defined conditions (e.g., a verified customer request or troubleshooting) is common and defensible — but the spec and any customer-facing disclosure should reflect the real access model. Unrestricted support access would be the harder position, since it undercuts the customer-only promise and widens exposure of customer data.
If support cannot open reports, the spec is accurate and the main remaining item is confirming the 30-day retention is deliberate (data minimization) and documented. The one supporting question that matters most is the support-access one, because it determines whether the stated access promise is accurate and whether additional controls or disclosures are needed before launch:

Can support staff open customer account activity reports, and if so under what conditions?

No — only the customer can open reports; support cannot
Yes — support can open reports only under defined conditions (e.g., verified customer request, troubleshooting)
Yes — support can open reports without restriction
Not yet decided — business is still determining this I've recorded the reported facts and this question in the matter. Per your instruction, I have not recorded a legal decision or created a draft. Once you answer the support-access question, I can give a more concrete read on what (if anything) needs to change in the spec or disclosures before the pilot.
